record.notes: Introduced 16 June 2022 (first reading); second reading and referral to the Standing Committee on Industry and Technology 24 April 2023, with a separate vote on Part 3; last committee meeting 26 Sept 2024. The Artificial Intelligence and Data Act would have come into force on a day or days fixed by order of the Governor in Council (its section 41). The 1st Session of the 44th Parliament was prorogued on 6 Jan 2025, and government bills without royal assent ceased to exist, so the bill died at committee stage. No AIDA successor as of Oct 2026: the June 2026 National AI Strategy relies on privacy and online-safety law modernisation instead. Bill C-36 (Protecting Privacy and Consumer Data Act, first reading 15 June 2026, sponsored by the Minister of AI and Digital Innovation) re-enacts only the privacy part of C-27, including disclosure on automated decision systems.

verification.note: Stored: the bill's text at first reading (parl.ca PDF, 16 June 2022), from which Part 3 is summarised; the LEGISinfo page for C-27 (44-1), which gives the full title, first reading 16 June 2022, second reading and referral 24 April 2023, consideration in committee 'Not completed' and the end of the session on 6 Jan 2025; the House of Commons Speaker's news release of 6 Jan 2025 on the prorogation and its effect on government bills (ourcommons.ca, a host not yet listed in pipeline/official-sites.json); and ISED's archived AIDA page (modified 2025-12-09). The statements on Bill C-36 and the June 2026 strategy rest on the verification of 11 Oct 2026 (LEGISinfo 45-1/c-36), not on files stored in this run. A press report of late Sept 2026 quotes AI Minister Evan Solomon saying that AI deployment needs regulation, without details; no official source for it was stored.

judgment.status_reasoning: LEGISinfo (stored 11 Oct 2026) marks the page as relating to a prior session, gives the 1st session of the 44th Parliament as 22 Nov 2021 to 6 Jan 2025, and shows consideration in committee 'Not completed', report stage and third reading 'Not reached' and no Senate stage. The Speaker's release of 6 Jan 2025 says that the session was prorogued that day and that government bills without royal assent cease to exist. C-27 had not left committee, so it fell: 'Lapsed' stands, with legal_force 'Proposed' and date_last_updated 2025-01-06.
judgment.summary_check: The summary's account of Part 3 matches the bill's text: assessment of whether a system is high-impact (s. 7), risk mitigation (s. 8), monitoring (s. 9), records (s. 10), plain-language public descriptions (s. 11), notification of material harm (s. 12), the Artificial Intelligence and Data Commissioner (s. 33) and the offence of making available a system whose use causes serious harm (s. 39).
